solution: Because the reversed segment's endpoints carry the same character, the transitions just outside it are untouched and the transitions inside are only reordered, so the number of maximal runs and the first run's character are invariant; a reachable string is thus described entirely by its run-length composition. Picking l inside run i and r inside run j (same character, so j-i is even) moves an arbitrary amount of length between runs i and j while keeping both at least 1, and reverses the order of the runs strictly between them. Taking j = i+2 gives a free length transfer between two runs of one colour, and j = i+4 transposes two runs of the other colour while leaving the endpoints' lengths fixed, so the runs of each colour can independently take any composition of that colour's total length into its own number of runs. The answer is therefore C(c0-1, k0-1) * C(c1-1, k1-1) mod 998244353, where c_x counts characters x and k_x counts runs of x (an absent colour contributes a factor 1), computed with precomputed factorials in O(n) for n up to 1e6. Exhaustive BFS over the reachable set of every binary string of length up to 14 confirms the formula.
annotator: claude agent, verified against a brute force
notes: Formula C(c0-1,k0-1)*C(c1-1,k1-1) verified by exhaustive BFS on all 2^n binary strings for n <= 14. stars-and-bars is exact here: each colour's answer is the number of compositions of its total length into its number of runs with every part positive. The actual crux is an invariant argument on the run-length encoding (run count and leading character are preserved), and the vocabulary has no label for invariant-finding; combinatorics is the closest real label for the counting half. modular-arithmetic is listed only because n up to 1e6 makes precomputed factorials plus modular inverses genuine machinery, not a one-line mod.
